system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The system prompt is assembled in `agent/prompt.py` from modular sections.
system_prompt_style.note: AGENTS.md read from sandbox and injected into the system prompt.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: If the repo contains an `AGENTS.md` file at the root, it's read from the sandbox and injected into the system prompt.
env_context_strategy.note: Also agent-driven navigation via grep/rg/execute; issue/thread source context injected.

observation_format.evidence_quote: A `browser` subagent drives Chromium inside the task sandbox via the [Stagehand](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand-python) SDK
observation_format.note: raw_text from execute/file tools; browser subagent implies visual observation but format not stated.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The agent will automatically see the tool's name, docstring, and parameter types — the docstring serves as the tool description

tool_count.note: README states ~15 curated tools: 4 custom tools in default list plus built-in Deep Agents file/shell/subagent tools.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The agent will automatically see the tool's name, docstring, and parameter types
tool_schema_source.note: MCP via Datadog hosted MCP server and Corridor MCP (opt-in).

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: the agent gains Datadog tools (via Datadog's hosted MCP server, default `toolsets=core`)
protocol_standardization.note: Opt-in server-side; also Corridor hosted MCP.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Deterministic middleware hooks run around the agent loop
loop_primitives.note: Deep Agents ReAct loop with middleware hooks; webhook-triggered runs.

planning_granularity.note: plan_mode middleware, enter_plan_mode/approve_plan/save_plan tools and plan_store exist; default mode not stated.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The main agent can fan out independent subtasks to isolated subagents — each with its own middleware stack and file operations.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The Deep Agents framework natively supports spawning child agents via the `task` tool.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Only use for local development with human-in-the-loop enabled.
human_in_loop.note: Default cloud sandbox: "No production access, no confirmation prompts." Workflow approval and approve_plan exist.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Each invocation creates a deterministic thread ID, so follow-up messages on the same issue or thread route to the same running agent.
short_term_state.note: LangGraph thread state with message queue; inferred.

long_term_memory.note: bundled_skills and organization_skills/user_skills tools; AGENTS.md file context.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Each thread gets a persistent sandbox (reused across follow-up messages)

self_verification.evidence_quote: The agent is instructed to run linters, formatters, and tests before committing
self_verification.note: Validation is prompt-driven, not harness-enforced; reviewer/analyzer graphs exist for PR review.

retry_policy.note: agent/middleware/task_retry.py exists but behaviour not described.

rollback.evidence_quote: commits changes and opens a draft PR when done, linked back to your ticket
rollback.note: Git branch/PR workflow; sandbox_reset/recreate_sandbox tools also present.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: **`notify_step_limit_reached`** — After-agent hook that posts a Slack reply when the agent hits the model-call limit

cost_controls.evidence_quote: You can route to different models based on task complexity, repo, or trigger source
cost_controls.note: Gateway adds central spend limits when enabled (off by default).

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Every task runs in its own **isolated cloud sandbox** — a remote Linux environment with full shell access.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: The repo is cloned in, the agent gets full permissions, and the blast radius of any mistake is fully contained.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Open SWE configures two GitHub proxy rules whenever a sandbox is created or reattached to a run
network_policy.note: Egress proxy injects credentials; README also says "the agent has network egress", so general egress appears open.

permission_model.evidence_quote: No production access, no confirmation prompts.
permission_model.note: Isolate first, then give full permissions inside the boundary.

tracing.note: LangSmith tracing is the run record.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Open SWE exposes only Corridor's `analyzePlan` tool.
guardrails.note: pr_creation_guard, workflow_push_guard, sanitize_tool_inputs middleware; Corridor guardrails opt-in.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Open-source framework for building your org's internal coding agent.
